1. Convert the observed line energy to frequency / wavelength  
   • E = 3.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV  
   • h = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV s  
   • ν = E/h ≈ (3.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV)/(4.14 × 10⁻¹⁵ eV s) ≈ 9.4 × 10⁸ Hz  
   • λ = c/ν ≈ (3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)/(9.4 × 10⁸ Hz) ≈ 0.32 m ≃ 32 cm.

2. Compare with well-known rest-frame lines  
   • The classic 21-cm (λ = 0.21 m, ν = 1.420 GHz) hyperfine transition of neutral hydrogen (H I) has rest-energy  
     E₀ = h ν₀ ≈ 5.9 μeV.

3. Account for cosmological redshift  
   • A source at D ≈ 2.1 Gpc corresponds to z ≈ H₀D/c ≃ 0.5 (for H₀ ≈ 70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹).  
   • The observed energy is therefore E_obs ≃ E₀/(1+z) ≃ 5.9 μeV / 1.5 ≃ 3.9 μeV, matching the given value.

   Hence the detected line is the redshifted 21-cm hyperfine transition of neutral atomic hydrogen.

4. In the Milky Way, the 21-cm line is produced predominantly by the cold neutral (atomic) interstellar medium (CNM), not by molecular gas or warm phases.

Therefore the most likely component traced by this absorption line in our Galaxy is:

Answer: C
